name: The Samatha Centre
tradition: Samatha-Vipassana tradition of Theravada Buddhism, rooted in the Thai Forest lineage brought to Britain by Nai Boonman
technique: Breathing-mindfulness (anapanasati) samatha meditation, taught developmentally in stages toward jhana and insight
influences: Pre-reform Thai/Southeast Asian Yogavacara jhana tradition
Acaan Mun and Luang Por Sodh lineages
teacherAccess: Group meetings, individual practice time, discussion, and one-to-one consultations with volunteer teachers throughout residential courses; teachers take no personal remuneration
retreatOptions: Weekend (Friday evening-Sunday) and week-long Introductory residential courses for newcomers; Intermediate residential courses for those who have learned the practice's 16 stages; also local weekly classes and online/Zoom courses
about: The Samatha Centre at Greenstreete is the national residential centre of the Samatha Trust, a Buddhist charity founded in 1973 to teach the Samatha-Vipassana meditation that the lay teacher Nai Boonman brought to Britain from Thailand in the 1960s, rooted in pre-reform Southeast Asian jhana practice. Set on an 88-acre former Welsh hill farm near Llangunllo and Knighton in Mid Wales, bought by the Trust in 1987, the centre has a converted farmhouse with individual accommodation, a purpose-built shrine hall and meditation hall, and forest meditation huts amid woodland, streams and a wetland created by members. It offers weekend and week-long residential Introductory courses teaching breathing-mindfulness meditation through group sessions, individual practice, discussion and one-to-one guidance, alongside Intermediate courses for more experienced practitioners. Members also pursue Pali chanting, textual study of the Abhidhamma, and land-management projects on the grounds. Teaching itself is always given freely; the Trust's wider activities, including local classes and Intermediate courses, run on voluntary donations, while Introductory residential courses carry a modest fixed fee.
schedule: Weekend Introductory courses run Friday evening to Sunday after lunch (about 2pm); week-long Introductory and Intermediate courses also held; days include group meditation sessions, talks, discussion, one-to-one teacher consultations, and a daily kitchen work period
cost: Teaching is always free; local classes and Intermediate residential courses are donation-only, while Introductory residential courses at Greenstreete charge a fixed two-tier fee (wage-earner vs. unwaged) payable six weeks in advance

pricePerDay.notes: Weekend Introductory Course (Friday evening to Sunday ~2pm, 2 nights, meals and accommodation included): Unwaged GBP 60 to Wage-earner GBP 120, i.e. GBP 30-60/night. The week-long Introductory course is GBP 100 unwaged/GBP 200 waged; Intermediate courses and local classes are donation-only with no fixed fee.

foodNotes: Meals are provided communally during residential courses and participants are generally asked to help in the kitchen; the site does not specify whether meals are vegetarian, vegan, or omnivore.
workNotes: Residential course participants are generally asked to help with kitchen duties, but this is a light communal chore rather than a formal work-retreat programme.
